item.title: Morning Video Frame Thumbnail

turns.text: Use a clear frame from my video to make a 16:9 YouTube thumbnail. Keep me recognisable and add “MORNINGS MADE EASY” in big letters beside my face. Pick the frame yourself; make it warm and upbeat.

item.tests: Tests extracting a usable frame from an attached video and composing it with readable text into a still thumbnail.

answer_sheet.Source and frame selection: Use talk-one.mp4; pick a clear frame yourself.
answer_sheet.Person: The woman speaking at the kitchen table in the attached video; keep her recognisable.
answer_sheet.Platform and size: One 16:9 YouTube thumbnail; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Visual style: Warm and upbeat, with big text beside my face; colours and font are your call.

must_haves: The deliverable is one still image in 16:9, not a video.
The thumbnail visibly uses a frame from talk-one.mp4, retaining the woman's identity and source-frame appearance.
The woman's face is clear and unobstructed.
The headline reads exactly “MORNINGS MADE EASY” in large, legible letters beside her face.
The overall treatment looks warm and upbeat.

turns.text: Could you use a clear frame from the attached clip to make a thumbnail for me, and pick the frame yourself rather than having me choose one? I’m hoping this will make the video feel a little more inviting when people first come across it. What I need is a 16:9 YouTube thumbnail, with me kept recognisable and the exact words “MORNINGS MADE EASY” in big letters beside my face. I always get a bit nervous about how I’ll look in a still pulled from a video. Please make the thumbnail warm and upbeat.

dialog.agent:
Absolutely—the aim is a warm, natural-looking still that still feels like you, with **“MORNINGS MADE EASY”** in large, readable letters beside your face.

There’s one technical snag: the connected tools can edit images, but they can’t extract full frames from your attached video. **Upload a few screenshots or a contact sheet from the clip, and I’ll pick the frame myself**—you don’t need to choose. I’ll look for open eyes, a relaxed expression and minimal motion blur, then make the 16:9 thumbnail while preserving your facial features.

Your free plan supports a 640px-wide result, which is below YouTube’s recommended 1280 × 720 size.
dialog.user: The source is talk-one.mp4, and I’d still like you to pick a clear frame yourself—the person to use is me, the woman speaking at the kitchen table. I don’t have screenshots or a contact sheet to provide here, so is there a way to work directly from the attached clip? Free-tier resolution is fine, and the colours and font are your call.

turns.agent:
I found a **portrait crop directly from your clip**, so you don’t need to provide screenshots. However, Magic Hour refused the thumbnail edit because your account has **insufficient credits**. No thumbnail was generated.

The prepared design uses your portrait on the left, a warm cream-and-peach background, and **“MORNINGS MADE EASY”** in large, dark-teal letters beside your face. It’s set to the free-tier 640px, 16:9 format.

Once credits are available, I can retry using that extracted portrait—no frame selection needed from you.

approvals.name: edit_image

style.prompt: Create a warm, upbeat 16:9 YouTube thumbnail using the supplied portrait crop taken from the user's video. Preserve this woman's recognisable identity and actual facial features, age, skin tone, hairstyle and natural appearance. Do not beautify, reshape her face or change her identity. Keep her face natural and relaxed, not exaggerated. Place her portrait large on the left side, comfortably framed with no clipping of the head. Use a clean warm cream background with soft peach and sunny golden accents and subtle morning-light warmth, inviting and uncluttered. On the RIGHT beside her face, render the exact words 'MORNINGS MADE EASY' in very large bold clean dark-teal sans-serif block lettering, arranged as MORNINGS / MADE / EASY. Spell every word exactly. High contrast, generous margins, legible at small YouTube thumbnail size. No other text, no logos, no watermark, no extra people. Use the supplied face as the identity reference, not a generic replacement person.
